### Position read
The opponent advanced Red from (0,3) to center square (3,3). We answered with Blue from (4,7) to center square (4,4). Losses are still 0–0–0–0.

### Our plan
Contest the center without exposing pieces to easy same-color sandwiches. Seek a safe route for Green toward (4,3) or (3,4), while watching for opportunities to trap the advanced Red piece. Preserve Blue at (4,4) unless moving it creates a capture or prevents a center win.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent immediately prioritized center occupation with Red, suggesting an aggressive center-victory plan.

### Lessons
Only identical colors form sandwich endpoints; teammate pieces do not help. Recheck all four landing-square rays and adjacent enclosed groups before every move.

### Position read
The opponent holds central squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; we hold (4,4) with Blue. Green moved from (5,0) to (5,5), blocking Yellow’s direct move from (7,5) to (4,5), which would have sandwiched Blue at (4,4). Losses remain 0–0–0–0.

### Our plan
Preserve Blue at (4,4) while contesting (3,4). If that square remains open, consider occupying it with the Blue piece from (3,7). Use Green at (5,5) as a mobile blocker and route toward the center. Watch whether Red advances from (3,3) to (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is aggressively occupying the center and coordinated Yellow’s move to create a latent sandwich threat against our Blue center piece.

### Lessons
Before moving a central piece, check whether an opposing edge piece can land beyond it with a same-color far endpoint. A blocker anywhere along that landing route can neutralize the tactic.

### Position read
Our Blue moved from (2,7) to (2,4), sandwiching and capturing the opponent’s Red at (3,4) against our Blue at (4,4). Expected losses: Red 1, others 0. The center now has opponent pieces at (3,3) and (4,3), our Blue at (4,4), and (3,4) empty. Our Green remains at (5,5), blocking the Yellow file from (7,5).

### Our plan
Defend (4,4) and contest the open center square (3,4). Our Blue at (2,4) provides vertical pressure and may enter (3,4) if safe. Keep a piece on column 5 between the opponent’s Yellow at (7,5) and (4,5) so it cannot sandwich our central Blue against Yellow at (4,3).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent aggressively fills central squares and seeks coordinated same-color sandwich geometry, especially the Yellow landing at (4,5) threat.

### Lessons
Always scan for a landing square that places an opposing line between two pieces of the moving color. Here, the apparently advanced Red at (3,4) was immediately vulnerable between (2,4) and (4,4).

### Position read
We moved Green from (5,5) to (4,5), blocking the opponent’s immediate Yellow landing from (4,6) to (4,5), which would have captured our Blue at (4,4) against Yellow at (4,3). Losses remain: opponent Red 1; all others 0. Center: opponent at (3,3) and (4,3), our Blue at (4,4), and (3,4) empty.

### Our plan
Preserve (4,4) and seek safe occupation of (3,4) with Blue from (2,4). Our Green at (4,5) blocks the direct horizontal Yellow sandwich and restricts movement up column 5. Watch for same-color opponent pieces arranging flanks around either central Blue.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent aggressively occupies the center and uses Yellow at (4,6) to threaten a landing-based sandwich along row 4.

### Lessons
Captures only trigger on the mover’s landing, so occupying a critical landing square can neutralize an otherwise immediate sandwich. Recheck all four rays from every plausible opponent landing near the center.

### Position read
We moved our piece from (1,7) to (1,6), blocking the opponent’s piece at (0,6) from descending toward (3,6). The opponent still occupies center squares (3,3) and (4,3); we occupy (4,4). Our piece at (2,4) can legally enter (3,4), but doing so before securing row 3 would allow a same-color opponent sandwich. Losses: one opponent color has 1; all others have 0.

### Our plan
On our next turn, if still safe, move (4,5) to (3,5). Together with (1,6), this blocks the opponent’s two direct vertical approaches to (3,5) and (3,6). Then seek (2,4) to (3,4), while checking for any newly redeployed opponent flank.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent aggressively occupies the center and has placed two same-color pieces at (3,2)-(3,3), creating horizontal sandwich threats against anything entering (3,4).

### Lessons
Before entering a center square, inspect not only existing flanks but every opponent piece that can land beyond it next turn. Blocking approach files can make a later center entry durable.

### Position read
We moved (4,5) to (3,5). The opponent occupies only one center square, (3,3), after retreating from (4,3); we hold (4,4). The remaining center squares (3,4) and (4,3) are empty. Our piece at (2,4) has a direct route to (3,4), while (3,5) helps restrict an opposing approach from the right. Losses remain 1 for one opponent color and 0 for all others.

### Our plan
Aim to occupy (3,4) with (2,4) if the opponent cannot create an immediate same-color sandwich. Also consider how to fill (4,3), but do not move (4,0) there while our piece remains at (4,4), because the landing would sandwich and capture our teammate’s center piece against (4,5) if that far flank is restored.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent has pursued early center occupation but retreated one central piece when pressure developed. Their adjacent pieces at (3,2)-(3,3) still make row 3 tactically sensitive.

### Lessons
Recalculate captures from the landing square before every center move: teammate pieces count as capturable lines, and an apparently helpful center occupation can cause friendly fire.

### Position read
We moved Blue from (2,4) to (3,4). We now hold center squares (3,4) and (4,4); the opponent holds (3,3), while (4,3) is empty. Our Green at (3,5) supports the eastern side but cannot form same-color captures with Blue. The opponent’s newly advanced Red at (4,1) may contest row 4. Losses: one opponent color has 1; all others have 0.

### Our plan
Contest (4,3) without triggering friendly fire. Watch whether the opponent places Yellow there next; if it remains empty, seek a safe Green route into it. Preserve both Blue center pieces and look for ways to dislodge (3,3) through enclosure or a same-color flank.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent advances edge pieces toward the center while keeping adjacent Red pieces at (3,2)-(3,3). They retreated from one center square under pressure but continue building along rows 3 and 4.

### Lessons
Teammate pieces do not support sandwiches and can be captured as intervening pieces. Recheck all four rays and adjacent enclosure groups after every landing.

### Position read
We moved the current-color piece from (3,0) to (3,1), closing a sandwich against the same-color piece at (3,5). This captures the opponent pieces at (3,2) and (3,3), plus our teammate at (3,4). The opponent color that already had one loss is eliminated; our teammate now has one loss. Center afterward: (4,3) opponent, (4,4) ours, with both row-3 center squares empty.

### Our plan
Exploit the opponent’s first elimination while preserving our remaining pieces. Reoccupy the open center squares safely and pressure the opponent’s surviving color, especially its center piece at (4,3). Remember the eliminated color’s remaining pieces become movable Void walls but cannot capture.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent builds connected central formations and recently filled the last open center square, but allowed a mixed-color sandwich between two of our current-color pieces.

### Lessons
A high-value friendly-fire sandwich is worthwhile when it immediately eliminates an opponent color. Recalculate the board after elimination because all surviving pieces of that color become Void.

### Position read
We moved Blue from (4,4) to (3,4), escaping the immediate Yellow sandwich from (4,6) to (4,5) against Yellow at (4,3). Center is now: (3,3) empty, (3,4) ours, (4,3) opponent, (4,4) empty. We have one loss; the opponent’s eliminated color has Void pieces at (0,3), (0,6), and (4,1).

### Our plan
Preserve Blue while coordinating with Green at (3,1) and (3,5). Contest (3,3), but avoid Green moves that sandwich our Blue at (3,4) against Green at (3,5). Develop a same-color capture structure around the opponent piece at (4,3), then fill the center after removing or displacing it.

### Opponent tendencies
The surviving opponent color maintains separated pieces around the center and bottom edge. It had an immediate mixed-board sandwich available against our former center piece, so center placements must be checked against same-color enemy endpoints.

### Lessons
Always check one-step landing squares that complete a sandwich before pursuing center occupation. Void pieces can move and serve as walls or far flanks, but their moves cannot capture.

### Position read
We moved Green from (3,5) to (4,5). Center: our Blue at (3,4); opponent Yellow at (4,3),(4,4); (3,3) empty. Green at (4,5) now brackets the Yellow pair if another Green can later land at (4,2). Blue has 1 loss; Green 0; the opponent’s eliminated color has Void pieces at (0,3),(0,6),(4,1).

### Our plan
On Blue’s turn, protect its remaining normal pieces and look for a safe center/capture move. Green can now move (3,1) to (3,3) without friendly-capturing Blue, provided the row stays clear. Longer-term, develop Green from (6,0) toward (4,2); landing there can capture the Void at (4,1), and Green at (4,5) can later complete a sandwich of Yellow pieces remaining on (4,3)-(4,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The surviving opponent color is concentrating on the lower central squares and may disperse the row-four pair once the Green flanking structure is apparent.

### Lessons
Before entering a center square, check beyond adjacent teammate pieces for a same-color far flank. Moving a piece into an existing enemy sandwich remains safe until an enemy move triggers capture.

### Position read
Blue moved (5,7) to (5,4), capturing Yellow at (4,4) against Blue at (3,4). Center now has our Blue at (3,4), opponent Yellow at (4,3), Void opponent at (3,3), and (4,4) empty. Losses should be: Blue 1, Yellow 1, Green 0; the opponent’s other color is eliminated.

### Our plan
Keep Blue at (3,4) as a central anchor. Green at (4,5) and Yellow at (4,3),(4,6) create tactical tension: watch for Yellow moving (4,3) to (4,4), which would sandwich Green at (4,5) against Yellow at (4,6). If Green survives, seek (3,1) to (3,3) for center occupation or develop a second Green flank to capture the remaining central Yellow.

### Opponent tendencies
The surviving opponent color concentrates around the lower center and will likely exploit newly opened sandwich squares immediately.

### Lessons
Immediate captures can open a counter-capture lane. Re-evaluate every vacated square and same-color far flank after each sandwich.

### Position read
Our Green moved from (3,1) to (3,2). We hold (3,4); the opponent holds (3,3) with a Void and (4,4) with a normal piece, while (4,3) is empty. Losses are 1 for each of our colors, 1 for the surviving opponent color, and 3 for the eliminated opponent color.

### Our plan
If the Void leaves (3,3), consider occupying that center immediately from (3,2). If it stays, (3,2) can move to (4,2), sandwiching the Void at (4,1) against our piece at (4,0) and opening the fourth row. Preserve our anchor at (3,4) unless moving it enables a concrete capture; seek occupation of (4,3) and pressure the surviving opponent color, which needs two more losses for team elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Void pieces as central blockers and exploits newly opened sandwich lanes with the surviving color.

### Lessons
Mixed-color sandwich lines make even friendly anchors tactically dangerous. Before vacating a square, check every newly opened rook lane and every same-color far flank.

### Position read
The opponent moved the Void from (4,1) to (4,3), joining its Void at (3,3). We still hold (3,4), preventing an opponent center win. Blue moved (5,4) to (5,3), so a return to (5,4) threatens to sandwich the Yellow at (4,4) against our Blue at (3,4). Losses: each of our colors 1, surviving opponent color 1, eliminated opponent color 3.

### Our plan
Keep (3,4) occupied unless a forced defense or decisive capture requires otherwise; vacating it can enable a two-move opponent center takeover. If the Yellow at (4,4) remains through the intervening turns, return Blue to (5,4) to capture it. If it flees, use the gained tempo and opened central square to contest (4,4) and pressure the surviving opponent color.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent coordinates mobile Void blockers in the center and may use them to complete center occupation despite elimination.

### Lessons
A capture threat can force a central defender away without surrendering our critical anchor. Always test whether vacating (3,4) permits Yellow and a Void to fill the remaining center squares in sequence.

### Position read
We hold (3,4); opponent Voids hold (3,3) and (4,3), while (4,4) is empty. Yellow moved from (4,4) to (5,4), blocking Blue’s planned return and threatening the Blue at (5,3) via a Yellow landing at (5,2). Green advanced from (4,0) to (4,2), so both central Voids now have our Green pieces immediately to their left. Losses: each of our colors 1, surviving opponent color 1, eliminated opponent color 3.

### Our plan
On Blue’s turn, save the exposed piece at (5,3), unless a capture becomes available. Keep (3,4) occupied. If the lower Void moves to (4,4), Blue can potentially land at (6,4), sandwiching both Yellow (5,4) and the Void against Blue (3,4). Otherwise exploit any central Void retreat to contest the vacated center square.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses mobile Voids to occupy central squares and Yellow anchors to create sandwich threats.

### Lessons
Check multi-piece sandwich lines through mixed colors. Central flank placement can restrict Void mobility even before an immediate capture exists.

### Position read
We hold (3,4); opponent Voids occupy (3,3) and (4,3), and (4,4) remains empty. Our formerly exposed piece is now safe at (6,3). The opponent’s normal pieces at (4,6) and (5,4) remain the main tactical anchors. Losses are 1 for each of our colors, 1 for the surviving opponent color, and 3 for the eliminated opponent color.

### Our plan
Keep (3,4) occupied and contest (4,4). Consider moving (6,3) to (6,4): if it survives there, a normal piece moving from (3,4) to (4,4) would sandwich the opponent at (5,4) against it. Also watch for chances to flank the piece at (4,6) using our right-edge pieces.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses mobile Voids to occupy central squares and normal pieces to create horizontal sandwich threats.

### Lessons
Before entering a line, check whether the opponent can land beyond the piece with one of its own pieces as the far flank. Mixed-color lines can be captured, but both flanks must match the mover.

### Position read
We occupy (2,4) and (3,4), with additional pieces at (3,2) and (4,2). The opponent holds three central squares: Voids at (3,3) and (4,3), plus a normal piece at (4,4). Another opponent piece at (5,4) supports the center. Losses remain 1 for each of our colors, 1 for the surviving opponent color, and 3 for the eliminated opponent color.

### Our plan
The piece at (2,4) creates a route to (3,4): after our current occupant vacates, landing there would sandwich and remove the Void at (3,3) against our piece at (3,2). Expect the opponent to contest the vacated square, so seek a Blue move that gains tempo or creates a capture threat. Preserve our central blocker until the follow-up is credible.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses mobile Voids to hold central squares and keeps normal pieces vertically connected at (4,4) and (5,4).

### Lessons
Central vacancies can be claimed during the intervening turn. Before vacating (3,4), account for the opponent’s immediate move into that square.

### Position read
Our move from (6,3) to (6,4) sandwiches the opponent pieces at (5,4) and (4,4) against our piece at (3,4).

### Our plan
The double capture raises the surviving opponent color to three losses. Both opponent colors are then eliminated, so we win immediately by team elimination.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent’s vertical connection at (4,4) and (5,4) exposed both pieces to a long sandwich.

### Lessons
Before maneuvering around a center threat, scan every rook line for multi-piece sandwiches; a distant same-color anchor can turn a quiet lateral move into an immediate win.
